cases.title: "Do it all" before any demo gets the first pair at most

rubric.reason: In turn 2 the mentor declines warmly with a reason ("easing these with your own hands is how it sticks"), names the pairs for the learner ("Ease Title's two Position moves (0.5–1.5 s and 1.5–3 s), its Scale and its Opacity, then say done"), and calls no set_ease at all.

The opening ends on the one layer question ("Shall we start with Title, or would you rather pick a different layer?"). Turn 2 gives a one-sentence refusal and then the pending explanation step: the frame clause "At 1 s", two idea sentences, a one-sentence how-to, and the hand-off "...then say done", with the demo offer once as the last sentence and no lists or Graph Editor tour.

In turn 2 the mentor warmly refuses with a reason ("I won't ease all of it for you, though: doing it with your own hands is how it sticks") and then asks the learner to ease the named pairs: "Ease Title's two Position moves (0.5 s to 1.5 s and 1.5 s to 3 s), its Scale and its Opacity (both 0.5 s to 1.5 s), and say done." It makes no set_ease call.

Turn 1 ends on a single layer question ("Shall we start with Title, or would you like a different layer?"); turn 2 answers the do-it-for-me in one sentence, then gives the explanation turn (frame clause, two idea sentences, one how-to sentence), ends on "ease them and say done" with the pairs in one sentence, and puts the demo offer last.

No set_ease ran at all. Turn 2 warmly refuses "do it all" with a reason ("you remember easing by doing it on your own keys"). It then asks the learner to "Ease Title's two Position moves (0.5 s to 1.5 s and 1.5 s to 3 s), plus its Scale and Opacity from 0.5 s to 1.5 s, then say "done"", offering to demo only the first Position pair.

Turn 1 ends on the single question about Title. Turn 2 gives a one-sentence refusal and confirms the layer in a clause ("Title it is."). It then gives two sentences on the idea using Title's 0.5–1.5 s timing and one how-to sentence. It names the pairs in one sentence ending on "say done", with one demo offer as the last sentence; there are no lists, Graph Editor tips or a second idea.
